statement: Type : Multiple Choice Question An arrangement of the masses and pulleys is shown in the figure. Strings connecting masses A and B with pulleys are horizontal and all pulleys and strings are light. Friction coefficient between the surface and the block B is 0.2 and between blocks A and B is 0.7. The system is released from rest. (use g=10 m/s2 ) 1 The magnitude of acceleration of the system is 2 m/s2 and there is no slipping between block A and block B. 50% Marked this option 2 The magnitude of friction force between block A and block B is 42 N. 50% Marked this option 3 Acceleration of block C is 1 m/s2 downwards. 25% Marked this option 4 Tension in the string connecting block B and block D is 12 N. 50% Marked this option You have missed this option 25% of students got it right Solution Hard Show Video Sol. For block C 60 – T = 6a      ……………(1) For Block D T ′ – 10 = a      …………….(2) Assume block A & B as a system, making FBD. (we can neglect the internal friction force between A and B . T−T'−f'=(6+3)a ⇒T−T'−0.2(6+3)g=9a ⇒T−T'=1.8g+9a……..(3) From eqn. (1) and (2) and (3) we get 6g−6a−(g+a)=T−T' i.e 6g−6a−g−a=1.8g+9a( from (3)) ⇒5g−7a=1.8g+9a ⇒a=2 m/s2 Now, for block A, T – f = 6 × a From eq. (1), 6(g−a)−f=6a 6×10−12×2=f ⇒f=36N Maximum friction force that can act between block A and block B =μ(mg)=0.7×(6×10)=42N=fmax Since, f<fmax, so both the blocks will move together without slipping. Hence our assumption was correct.

subject: Physics
topic: Coupled Masses Friction & Minimum Force to Hold
statement: Two masses m1=5 kg and m2=10 kg, connected by an inextensible string over a frictionless pulley, are moving as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction of horizontal surface is 0.15. The minimum weight m that should be put on top of m2 to stop the motion is : 1 23.3kg 49.71% Marked this option 2 43.3kg 24.43% Marked this option 3 10.3kg 18.68% Marked this option 4 18.3kg 7.47% Marked this option 49.14% of students got it right Solution Medium Show Video Sol. To completely stop the downward motion of mass m1, the maximum static friction force acting on the horizontal surface must be greater than or equal to the tension created by m1. Condition for equilibrium: fstatic≥T Where: Tension, T=m1g Frictional force, fstatic=μN=μ(m2+m)g Equating the forces: μ(m2+m)g≥m1g μ(m2+m)≥m1 Substituting the given values (m1=5 kg, m2=10 kg, μ=0.15): 0.15(10+m)≥5 10+m≥50.15 10+m≥33.33 m≥23.33 kg Conclusion The minimum mass required to stop the motion is mathematically 23.33 kg.
solutionText: To completely stop the downward motion of mass m1, the maximum static friction force acting on the horizontal surface must be greater than or equal to the tension created by m1.  Condition for equilibrium: fstatic≥T  Where:  Tension, T=m1g  Frictional force, fstatic=μN=μ(m2+m)g  Equating the forces: μ(m2+m)g≥m1g μ(m2+m)≥m1  Substituting the given values (m1=5 kg, m2=10 kg, μ=0.15): 0.15(10+m)≥5 10+m≥50.15 10+m≥33.33 m≥23.33 kg   Conclusion  The minimum mass required to stop the motion is mathematically 23.33 kg.

subject: Physics
topic: Contact Force between Accelerating Adjacent Blocks
statement: Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 1 kg are in contact with each other on a frictionless table. When a horizontal force of 3.0 N is applied to the block of mass 2 kg, the value of the force of contact between the two blocks is:
solutionText: Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 1 kg in contact. Horizontal force F = 3.0 N applied to 2 kg block. Common acceleration a = F / (m1 + m2) = 3.0 / (2 + 1) = 1.0 m/s^2. Contact force on 1 kg block = m2 * a = 1 kg * 1.0 m/s^2 = 1.0 N.
